Title: [Search][Request] Verify a valid multi-field Search request returns a non-empty offers array for a supported route.
Capabilities / Test Data: Supplier_Name=TravelportNdc, Credentials_Selector=UAE (or any pair confirmed live-capable per section 4.7); searchCriteria=[{origin:CAI,destination:JED,date:<future date>}]; passengers=[{ADT,2},{CHD,1},{INF,1}]; V1 POST api/FlightSearch/Search, V2 POST api/V2/FlightSearch/Search
Preconditions: Supplier/credentialsSelector pair confirmed technically reachable; STAG_ENV baseUrl selected; valid x-api-key/Client-Id headers set
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST with supplier, credentialsSelector, searchCriteria (origin/destination/date), passengers (ADT/CHD/INF counts) -> inspect response
Expected Result: HTTP 200; offers[] non-empty; every offer carries offerId, priceDetails, and haveBundles/canBeHeld/offerHasAncillary/isSeatMapRequired flags; responseId present and usable downstream as searchResponseId (V1) / ResponseId (V2)
Notes: Both versions share body shape and business purpose; only the URL path casing (V2 vs v2 is not an issue here, Search uses V2 in both) and downstream field name (searchResponseId vs ResponseId) differ, and that difference surfaces at FareConfirm, not at Search itself.

Title: [Search][Request] Validate Search request is rejected when the supplier field is omitted.
Capabilities / Test Data: Otherwise-valid Search body with the supplier key removed entirely; both V1 api/FlightSearch/Search and V2 api/V2/FlightSearch/Search
Preconditions: Valid credentialsSelector and searchCriteria/passengers present
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST body with supplier field omitted -> observe response
Expected Result: Request rejected; exact status code and body shape UNKNOWN per section 7.9 -- confirm live and record as the baseline for this class of missing-required-field test.
Notes: Error-response envelope is not yet characterized anywhere in either collection; use section 7.9's dedicated characterization case (TC-VERSIONDIFF-NEG-01) as the authority once run.

Title: [Search][Request] Validate Search request is rejected when searchCriteria is omitted.
Capabilities / Test Data: Otherwise-valid Search body with searchCriteria array removed entirely; both versions
Preconditions: Valid supplier/credentialsSelector/passengers present
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST body with searchCriteria omitted -> observe response
Expected Result: Request rejected; exact status code/body UNKNOWN, confirm live.
Notes: Same missing-required-field pattern as supplier; consolidate the generic field-omission sweep across both fields once error shape is confirmed.

Title: [Search][Request] Validate Search behavior for an invalid or lowercase IATA origin/destination code.
Capabilities / Test Data: origin='XXX' (invalid code) and, separately, origin='cai' (lowercase valid code); both versions
Preconditions: Valid supplier/credentialsSelector/passengers present
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST with an unrecognized IATA code, then separately with a lowercase valid code -> observe response for each
Expected Result: UNKNOWN whether an invalid code 4xx's or returns an empty offers[] 200; case-sensitivity of IATA codes is also UNKNOWN -- confirm both live.
Notes: A route the supplier does not fly is expected to be a valid negative/boundary test returning zero offers rather than an error, per section 2.1 -- distinguish that scenario from a genuinely malformed code in the write-up.

Title: [Search][Request] Validate Search accepts a total passenger count of exactly 9 (ADT+CHD+INF combined).
Capabilities / Test Data: passengers e.g. ADT=7,CHD=1,INF=1 (any mix summing to 9); both V1 and V2 Search
Preconditions: Valid supplier/credentialsSelector/searchCriteria
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST with passenger counts summing to exactly 9 -> observe response
Expected Result: HTTP 200; offers returned normally; no passenger-count rejection at the confirmed upper bound.
Notes: Reuses SPEC.md's own worked example shape (max = 9 confirmed hard business rule, not inferred).

Title: [Search][Request] Validate Search rejects a total passenger count of 10, one over the confirmed 9-passenger maximum.
Capabilities / Test Data: passengers summing to 10 (e.g. ADT=8,CHD=1,INF=1); both versions
Preconditions: Valid supplier/credentialsSelector/searchCriteria
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST with passenger counts summing to 10 -> observe response
Expected Result: Rejected; exact rejection point (4xx at Search itself vs accepted-then-rejected downstream) is UNKNOWN -- confirm live and record.
Notes: Primary negative/boundary counterpart to TC-SEARCH-BND-01; this is the confirmed hard business rule's over-the-limit case.

Title: [Search][Response] Verify Search response's supplier field matches the request's supplier value verbatim.
Capabilities / Test Data: Any valid Search request; both versions
Preconditions: Valid Search request executed
Steps / Endpoint Chain: supplier field on the response equals the supplier value sent in the request, unchanged
Expected Result: supplier is echoed back unchanged; no silent normalization/casing change.
Notes: credentialsSelector is not part of the observed Search response shape in either version -- this echo-consistency check applies to supplier only at this endpoint; credentialsSelector round-trip is better tested at an endpoint whose response does echo it, if one is found live.

Title: [Search][Response] Verify the per-passenger-type price-reconciliation formula holds on every returned Search offer.
Capabilities / Test Data: Any valid, multi-passenger-type Search response; both versions
Preconditions: Search returns at least one offer with a full passengerFareBreakdown
Steps / Endpoint Chain: For each offer: sum(taxesAndFees[].amount.amount) == paxTotalTaxAmount.amount; sum((paxBaseAmount+taxes)*paxCount) reconciles to priceDetails.totalAmount.amount; totalBaseAmount == sum(paxBaseAmount*paxCount); totalTaxAmount == sum(taxes*paxCount)
Expected Result: All four reconciliation checks hold for every offer and every passenger type present.
Notes: V1 Search's test script enforces this automatically; V2 Search's script does NOT (it only sets searchResponseId/offerId) -- manual testing must independently supply this check for V2 Search since automation will not catch a drift there.

Title: [Search][Request] Verify isdebug=true on Search exposes raw supplierRequest/supplierResponse fields, and confirm whether isdebug=false or omitted suppresses them.
Capabilities / Test Data: Same otherwise-valid Search request sent three ways: isdebug=true, isdebug=false, isdebug omitted; repro against AirArabia (the supplier with the observed finding) plus at least one other supplier; both versions
Preconditions: Access to a non-production environment for this test; awareness that a positive result must be escalated immediately
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] POST with isdebug=true -> inspect supplierRequest/supplierResponse; repeat with isdebug=false; repeat with isdebug omitted -> compare presence/absence of the two fields across all three runs
Expected Result: With isdebug=true, supplierRequest/supplierResponse are present and may contain raw upstream SOAP/XML; the AirArabia observed example's supplierResponse contained apparent live supplier SOAP credentials (wsse:Username/wsse:Password) in plaintext -- any such exposure must be flagged explicitly. Behavior of isdebug=false/omitted is UNKNOWN and must be confirmed live.
Notes: The single most concrete security finding in the whole spec. Escalate any confirmed plaintext-credential exposure to the security/dev team immediately regardless of this test case's pass/fail status; also confirm whether this response data is logged or cached downstream.

Title: [Search][Response] Verify Search response schema matches the baseline [Observed example] shape with no unexpected field removal, rename, or retype.
Capabilities / Test Data: Baseline: the section 2.1 [Observed example, V2] response shape; both versions compared against their own prior known-good run
Preconditions: A previously captured known-good Search response exists as the regression baseline
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Run Search -> diff every top-level and nested key (responseId, supplier, journeys, flightSegments, priceClasses, baggageDetails, offers[] and its nested fields, supplierRequest/supplierResponse when isdebug=true) against the baseline for presence and type
Expected Result: Schema matches the baseline exactly; any drift (field renamed, removed, or retyped) is reported as a regression even if the flow otherwise passes.
Notes: V1 has no saved example response at all in the collection (response:[] on every V1 request) -- V1's baseline must be captured from a live run rather than an existing example.

Title: [FareConfirm][Request] Verify FareConfirm returns a re-priced selectedOffer for a valid same-call responseId + selectedOfferId pair.
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 body uses searchResponseId; V2 body uses ResponseId (capital R) for the identical semantic value from Search's responseId; both also send selectedOfferId; V1 POST api/FlightSearch/FareConfirm, V2 POST api/v2/FlightSearch/FareConfirm
Preconditions: A prior Search call returned a responseId and at least one offerId from the same supplier/credentialsSelector pair
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] -> [FareConfirm] POST with the same-call responseId/offerId pair -> inspect selectedOffer
Expected Result: HTTP 200; selectedOffer present with offerId, priceDetails, refundability; V2 additionally carries haveBundles/canBeHeld/isAncillaryRequired/offerHasAncillary/isBaggageRequired/isMealRequired/isSeatMapRequired flags not present in V1's shape.
Notes: V2's six capability flags should be explicitly asserted even though the V2 collection's own script does not check them -- they are the pivot point for every downstream V2 branch.

Title: [FareConfirm][Request] Validate FareConfirm rejects a responseId + selectedOfferId pair originating from two different Search calls.
Capabilities / Test Data: Run Search twice (Search-A, Search-B) against the same supplier/credentialsSelector; build a FareConfirm request using Search-A's responseId with Search-B's offerId; both versions
Preconditions: Two independent Search responses available
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search-A], [Search-B] -> [FareConfirm] POST mixing Search-A's responseId with Search-B's selectedOfferId -> observe response
Expected Result: Expected to 4xx or return a supplier-level 'offer no longer available'-style error; exact behavior UNKNOWN, confirm live -- high-value negative test per section 1.7.
Notes: This is the general mismatched-ID class named explicitly in section 2.2's Negative Cases.

Title: [FareConfirm][Request] Validate V1's searchResponseId and V2's ResponseId field names are each accepted only under their own version's contract, not interchangeably.
Capabilities / Test Data: Send a V1 FareConfirm body using ResponseId instead of searchResponseId; separately send a V2 FareConfirm body using searchResponseId instead of ResponseId
Preconditions: Valid Search output available for both versions
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm] V1 POST with ResponseId substituted for searchResponseId -> observe; [FareConfirm] V2 POST with searchResponseId substituted for ResponseId -> observe
Expected Result: Both cross-version field-name substitutions are rejected or the field is ignored/treated as missing (exact behavior UNKNOWN, confirm live) -- this is a genuine contract difference, not a typo, and must not be treated as interchangeable.
Notes: This naming pattern recurs on V2's Upselling, GetOfferBundles, and AddPassenger calls too, all using ResponseId/PascalCase-leaning keys vs V1's camelCase.

Title: [Search]&[FareConfirm] [Response] Verify capability flags (haveBundles/canBeHeld/offerHasAncillary/isSeatMapRequired) stay consistent between Search and FareConfirm for the same offer.
Capabilities / Test Data: Same offerId carried from Search into FareConfirm; both versions
Preconditions: Search response includes the relevant capability flags for the selected offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] -> record flags on offers[selected] -> [FareConfirm] -> record the same flags on selectedOffer -> compare
Expected Result: Flags match between the two responses for the same offer; a flag flipping between steps is itself a defect worth reporting, not expected behavior.
Notes: Live per-offer flags take precedence over the static section 4.2 supplier matrix when the two disagree -- this test is the mechanism that surfaces such disagreements.

Title: [Search]&[FareConfirm] [Response] Verify Search's responseId and offers[0].offerId hand off correctly into FareConfirm's required fields.
Capabilities / Test Data: Search response's responseId/offerId; both versions' field-name mapping (searchResponseId+selectedOfferId for V1, ResponseId+selectedOfferId for V2)
Preconditions: Valid Search response available
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] -> map responseId/offerId into FareConfirm's request fields per version -> [FareConfirm] POST -> confirm success
Expected Result: FareConfirm succeeds using only Search's own output, with no manual field substitution beyond the documented name mapping.
Notes: This is the baseline two-endpoint hand-off integration test that every flow in section 5 depends on.

Title: [FareConfirm][Request] Validate FareConfirm behavior when confirming an offer whose underlying inventory sold out between Search and FareConfirm.
Capabilities / Test Data: A Search result for a low-availability/high-demand route/date, re-confirmed after a deliberate short delay; both versions
Preconditions: Ability to reproduce or simulate a realistic sold-out race condition
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] -> wait -> [FareConfirm] on the same offer -> observe response
Expected Result: Expected to surface as a distinct 'offer unavailable'-style error rather than a generic 500; exact shape UNKNOWN, confirm live.
Notes: Hard to force deterministically; treat as an opportunistic/exploratory test rather than a guaranteed-reproducible regression case.

Title: [GetOfferBundles][Request] Verify GetOfferBundles returns bundleChoices for an offer with haveBundles=true.
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 POST api/bundles/GetOfferBundles with fareConfirmResponseId+selectedOfferId; V2 POST api/V2/bundles/GetOfferBundles with ResponseId+selectedOfferId
Preconditions: Prior FareConfirm (or Upselling) call returned haveBundles=true for the selected offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm] (haveBundles=true) -> [GetOfferBundles] POST -> inspect bundleChoices/offerJourneys
Expected Result: bundleChoices populated with bundleCode/bundleName/bundlePrices/includedServices per bundle; offerJourneys is a map keyed by segmentRefId, each with a bundleReferences array.
Notes: Requires haveBundles=true on the prior FareConfirm/Upselling offer, per section 2.4's dependency.

Title: [GetOfferBundles][Request] Validate GetOfferBundles behavior when called for an offer with haveBundles=false.
Capabilities / Test Data: FareConfirm output where haveBundles=false; both versions
Preconditions: Prior FareConfirm call returned haveBundles=false for the selected offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm] (haveBundles=false) -> [GetOfferBundles] POST -> observe response
Expected Result: UNKNOWN exact result (empty bundleChoices vs explicit error) -- confirm live; a bundle-incapable offer should not silently return usable bundle data.
Notes: Valid negative/boundary test per section 2.4's Business Logic note.

Title: [GetOfferBundles][Response] Verify the JourneyKey1 script variable (resp.offerJourneys.key) is undefined against the real offerJourneys shape, in both V1 and V2 collections.
Capabilities / Test Data: Any GetOfferBundles success response; both versions
Preconditions: GetOfferBundles returns a valid bundleChoices/offerJourneys response
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [GetOfferBundles] POST -> evaluate resp.offerJourneys.key as the collection's own script does -> compare against the real keyed-by-segmentRefId shape
Expected Result: resp.offerJourneys.key evaluates to undefined since offerJourneys has no literal key property; JourneyKey1 does not appear to be consumed by any other request in either collection (likely a dead/inert variable), but the mismatch should still be reported as a script/response-shape defect.
Notes: Identically-worded bug in both V1 and V2 test scripts (var JourneyKey1 = resp.offerJourneys.key;) -- do not rely on JourneyKey1 for chaining in any flow test; thread fareConfirmResponseId/selectedOfferId through directly instead.

Title: [GetOfferBundles][Response] Validate bundleChoices keys are a subset of the bundleReferences listed per journey in offerJourneys.
Capabilities / Test Data: GetOfferBundles success response with multiple bundles; both versions
Preconditions: GetOfferBundles returns a non-empty bundleChoices object
Steps / Endpoint Chain: For each journey's bundleReferences entry, confirm a corresponding key exists in bundleChoices
Expected Result: Every bundleReferences code maps to a real bundleChoices entry; no orphaned references.

Title: [GetOfferBundles][Response] Validate includedServices mixes machine-readable tags with free-text rule strings, and known tags remain a subset rather than an exact-match set.
Capabilities / Test Data: GetOfferBundles success response; both versions
Preconditions: GetOfferBundles returns bundleChoices with includedServices populated
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Inspect includedServices array per bundle; check that known tags (BAGGAGE, MEAL, SEAT_MAP, FLEXI_CHARGES) appear as a subset, alongside free-text descriptions
Expected Result: Assertion passes as long as known tags are present as a subset; the array is not asserted to equal a fixed set, since human-readable rule strings coexist in the same array.
Notes: Response-shape quirk explicitly called out in the spec -- do not write a brittle exact-match assertion here.

Title: [Book][Request] Verify Book commits a confirmed offer to a live PNR and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR.
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 POST api/FlightBooking/Book with Supplier (capital S), fareConfirmResponseId, selectedOfferId, passengersList, contactsList, selectedBundles; V2 POST api/v2/FlightBooking/Book with ResponseId, selectedOfferId, PassengersSelectedAncillaries (no passengersList)
Preconditions: Non-production environment, OR explicit documented production-Book authorization obtained; valid FareConfirm (V1) / AddPassenger (V2) era IDs
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm]/[AddPassenger] -> [Book] POST -> inspect response
Expected Result: HTTP 200; pnr, bookingToken, gdsPNR non-empty; voidCapability present; passengersList is echoed in the RESPONSE for V2 even though absent from the V2 request (server resolves it from AddPassenger).
Notes: V1's request field is capital-S Supplier, inconsistent with every other V1 field's lowercase supplier -- note in test evidence, do not silently 'correct' it.

Title: [Book][Request] Validate behavior when booking twice with the same offer reference (double-booking attempt).
Capabilities / Test Data: Same fareConfirmResponseId/ResponseId + selectedOfferId reused across two Book calls; both versions
Preconditions: A single valid FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era ID pair
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Book] POST -> [Book] POST again with the identical offer reference -> observe both responses
Expected Result: UNKNOWN whether the second call is idempotently rejected or produces a second PNR -- confirm live; high-value negative test.

Title: [Book][Response] Verify the price-reconciliation formula holds on Book's response.
Capabilities / Test Data: Book success response with a full passengerFareBreakdown; both versions
Preconditions: Book returns a priced selectedOffer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Apply the section 2.1 reconciliation formula to Book's selectedOffer.priceDetails and passengerFareBreakdown
Expected Result: All reconciliation checks hold.
Notes: Enforced by script in V1 Book; absent from V2 Book's script -- manual testing must supply this check for V2.

Title: [Book][Request] Verify a Book call against a commercially blacklisted supplier/airline is blocked at the business layer.
Capabilities / Test Data: Blacklisted suppliers per section 4.3, e.g. FlyDubai, AirArabia (E5/G9/3L/3O), SereneAir, AirIndia, Indigo, AirBlue, Jazeera, FlyNas, AirCairo, FlyAdeal, SpiceJet, SalamAir, FlyJinnah; GLC is conditional not outright blocked; both versions
Preconditions: Search/FareConfirm succeed technically for the chosen blacklisted supplier
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Search] -> [FareConfirm] -> [Book] POST against the blacklisted supplier -> observe whether the booking-affecting action is blocked
Expected Result: Blocked/rejected at the business layer even though technically reachable through Search/FareConfirm; exact rejection mechanism UNKNOWN, confirm live. GLC specifically requires 'inform us first before issuing any ticket' rather than an outright block -- do not treat it identically to the outright-blacklisted suppliers.
Notes: Distinguishes technical capability (section 4.2) from commercial authorization (section 4.3) -- a supplier can pass Search/FareConfirm while being blocked here.

Title: [Book] Verify the production-booking auto-skip discipline is enforced as a manual process control before any Book/BookAfterHold execution against a production base URL.
Capabilities / Test Data: Checklist item, not a payload-driven test; applies to both V1 and V2 Book/BookAfterHold
Preconditions: N/A -- process/checklist control
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Before executing Book or BookAfterHold: (1) confirm environment classification (STAG vs PROD baseUrl); (2) if PROD, confirm explicit documented authorization exists; (3) proceed only if both are satisfied
Expected Result: No Book/BookAfterHold execution proceeds against a PROD baseUrl without explicit, documented authorization, regardless of Supplier_Name/Credentials_Selector configured.
Notes: This is a manual/process control, not automatable in Postman -- Postman has no environment guard equivalent to the adjacent automation framework's shouldSkipBookingInProduction; enforce via team checklist/review, not tooling.

Title: [Book][Request] Validate Book rejects a selectedOfferId that does not match the fareConfirmResponseId/ResponseId supplied in the same request.
Capabilities / Test Data: Mismatched selectedOfferId from a different FareConfirm response than the fareConfirmResponseId/ResponseId sent; both versions
Preconditions: Two independent FareConfirm responses for the same supplier
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm-A], [FareConfirm-B] -> [Book] POST mixing FareConfirm-A's responseId with FareConfirm-B's selectedOfferId -> observe response
Expected Result: Rejected; exact error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live.

Title: [Book][Request] Validate V1 Book's capital-S Supplier field is accepted consistently despite every other V1 field using lowercase supplier.
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 Book body with Supplier vs a deliberately lowercased supplier variant sent in its place; V1 only, but recorded here as the shared Book endpoint's field-naming concern
Preconditions: Valid V1 Book payload otherwise
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Book] V1 POST with Supplier (capital S) as documented -> observe; repeat with lowercase supplier substituted -> observe
Expected Result: Confirm live whether field-name matching is case-insensitive; if inconsistent handling is found, flag as a copy-paste artifact worth fixing in the collection.
Notes: V2's equivalent field is lowercase supplier consistently -- this is a V1-only naming inconsistency, not a V1/V2 contract difference, hence still in scope for this Both-version pass as a shared-endpoint concern.

Title: [Hold][Request] Verify Hold reserves an offer without immediate ticketing and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR plus holdExpirationDate.
Capabilities / Test Data: V1/V2 POST .../Hold; supplier confirmed canBeHeld=true via section 4.7 procedure; V2 note: saved example's credentialsSelector placeholder references {{credentialsSelector}} not {{Credentials_Selector}} -- must be corrected locally before running
Preconditions: Supplier confirmed canBeHeld=true for the selected offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm]/[AddPassenger] -> [Hold] POST -> inspect response
Expected Result: HTTP 200; pnr, bookingToken, gdsPNR non-empty; holdExpirationDate present and in the future.
Notes: V2's saved Hold request has a credentialsSelector casing/variable-reference defect ({{credentialsSelector}} vs the environment's actual {{Credentials_Selector}}) -- flag as a collection bug if reproduced, do not silently work around it without recording it.

Title: [Hold][Request] Validate Hold is rejected for a supplier/offer with canBeHeld=false (e.g. FlyNas, GLC).
Capabilities / Test Data: FlyNas or GLC (both sources agree canBeHeld=false for these two); both versions
Preconditions: FareConfirm/Search confirms canBeHeld=false for the chosen offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [FareConfirm] (canBeHeld=false) -> [Hold] POST -> observe response
Expected Result: Expected to fail; exact rejection shape UNKNOWN, confirm live. Per section 4.4, AirCairo/EgyptAir/Galileo/SpiceJet/GLC's Hold capability is disputed across sources -- trust the live canBeHeld flag over either static document when selecting suppliers for this case.
Notes: FlyNas and GLC are the two suppliers with the least ambiguous canBeHeld=false signal; use them here rather than the five disputed suppliers, which get their own dedicated CAPCHECK rows.

Title: [Hold][Response] Verify the price-reconciliation formula holds on Hold's response in both V1 and V2.
Capabilities / Test Data: Hold success response with a full passengerFareBreakdown; both versions
Preconditions: Hold returns a priced offer
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Apply the section 2.1 reconciliation formula to Hold's response
Expected Result: All reconciliation checks hold in both versions.
Notes: Hold is one of only two V2 booking-family endpoints (with FareConfirmAfterHold/BookAfterHold) that retained the price-check script, unlike V2's Book/Retrieve -- no coverage-gap caveat needed here, unlike TC-BOOK-BIZ-01.

Title: [Hold]&[FareConfirmAfterHold]&[BookAfterHold]&[CancelAfterHold] [Response] Verify behavior when FareConfirmAfterHold, BookAfterHold, or CancelAfterHold is attempted after the booking's holdExpirationDate has passed.
Capabilities / Test Data: A Held booking deliberately left past its holdExpirationDate before the next call; both versions
Preconditions: A Hold response with a known holdExpirationDate; ability to wait or otherwise reach a time past that timestamp
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] -> wait past holdExpirationDate -> [FareConfirmAfterHold] POST -> observe; repeat scenario independently for [BookAfterHold] and [CancelAfterHold]
Expected Result: UNKNOWN exact behavior for each of the three calls -- confirm live whether rejected outright or accepted with a price/availability re-check; applies identically in both versions and is not covered by any flow.md-listed flow number.
Notes: Timing-sensitive, hard to force deterministically on a schedule -- treat as an opportunistic/exploratory test rather than a routine regression case.

Title: [Retrieve][Response] Verify bookingStatus reflects the correct lifecycle stage (Held after Hold, Booked after Book/BookAfterHold).
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 POST api/FlightBooking/RetrieveBooking, V2 POST api/v2/FlightBooking/Retrieve; pnr/bookingToken/gdsPnr(gdsPNR) from a prior Hold or Book/BookAfterHold call
Preconditions: A completed Hold or Book/BookAfterHold call with known pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] or [Book] -> [Retrieve] POST with pnr/gdsPnr/bookingToken -> inspect bookingStatus
Expected Result: bookingStatus matches the expected lifecycle stage for the preceding action (record the actual observed string value as the regression baseline, since the full enumeration is UNKNOWN).
Notes: Retrieve's gdsPnr field casing differs from gdsPNR used elsewhere -- INFERRED cosmetic/case-insensitive, but note for exact-match request-shape tests.

Title: [Retrieve] Verify V2 Retrieve has zero test-script assertions, the largest single V1/V2 coverage gap of any endpoint.
Capabilities / Test Data: Compare V1 vs V2 Retrieve test scripts directly in the collections; run both against equivalent bookings
Preconditions: A completed booking retrievable in both a V1 and a V2 flow
Steps / Endpoint Chain: Inspect V1 Retrieve's script (price-reconciliation present) vs V2 Retrieve's script (no variable refs, no assertion titles) -> run both live and manually supply the missing checks for V2
Expected Result: Manual testing independently supplies the price-reconciliation and bookingStatus checks for V2 Retrieve, since V2's script provides none of what V1's does automatically.
Notes: This is a coverage gap, not a functional defect of the endpoint itself -- do not rely on 'the collection will catch it' for V2 Retrieve.

Title: [Retrieve][Response] Validate bookingStatus is one of the currently-known set, or flagged as a newly-observed value rather than hard-failed.
Capabilities / Test Data: Retrieve responses across as many distinct lifecycle stages as can be reached (Held, Booked, Voided, Cancelled); both versions
Preconditions: Bookings in multiple distinct lifecycle stages available to retrieve
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Retrieve] POST for a booking at each reachable lifecycle stage -> record the exact bookingStatus string observed each time
Expected Result: No full enumeration exists yet (UNKNOWN per section 8.3) -- this is a first-round exploratory priority; every distinct value observed must be recorded and fed back into SPEC.md's living-document update process rather than hard-failing on an unrecognized value.

Title: [Hold]&[Retrieve] [Response] Verify Retrieve immediately after Hold vs. after holdExpirationDate has passed returns the expected bookingStatus transition.
Capabilities / Test Data: A Held booking retrieved once promptly and once after its holdExpirationDate has passed; both versions
Preconditions: A Hold response with a known holdExpirationDate
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] -> [Retrieve] immediately -> record bookingStatus; [Hold] -> wait past holdExpirationDate -> [Retrieve] again -> record bookingStatus -> compare
Expected Result: Expected transition on expiry is UNKNOWN -- high-value exploratory test; record whatever is actually observed as the new baseline.

Title: [FareConfirmAfterHold][Response] Verify whether the reported price differs from the original Hold price after a hold-window delay (price-drift exploratory check).
Capabilities / Test Data: V1/V2 POST .../PnrReprice with pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName from a prior Hold; a deliberate delay between Hold and FareConfirmAfterHold
Preconditions: A Held booking with a known original price
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] -> record priceDetails.totalAmount -> wait -> [FareConfirmAfterHold] POST -> compare reported price against the original Hold price
Expected Result: In the common case, price should match with no drift; a mismatch is the price-drift scenario itself, not necessarily a bug -- report either outcome with the observed delta.
Notes: Requires a live environment where fares can plausibly move -- mark as an opportunistic/exploratory test rather than a deterministic regression case.

Title: [FareConfirmAfterHold][Request] Validate FareConfirmAfterHold behavior when called after the hold's holdExpirationDate has passed.
Capabilities / Test Data: A Held booking deliberately left past its holdExpirationDate; both versions
Preconditions: Hold response with a known holdExpirationDate
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] -> wait past holdExpirationDate -> [FareConfirmAfterHold] POST -> observe response
Expected Result: UNKNOWN -- expected to fail or return a price/availability change requiring re-acceptance; confirm live and record.
Notes: High-value exploratory/negative test per section 2.12's own Testing Notes.

Title: [Hold]&[BookAfterHold] [Response] Verify pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR returned by BookAfterHold equal the values established at Hold (same-PNR invariant).
Capabilities / Test Data: V1 POST .../BookAfterHold, V2 POST .../BookAfterHold (casing differs, functionally same); pnr/gdsPnr/bookingToken carried from Hold
Preconditions: A completed Hold (optionally re-confirmed via FareConfirmAfterHold) with known pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR
Steps / Endpoint Chain: [Hold] -> [FareConfirmAfterHold] -> [BookAfterHold] POST -> compare returned pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR against the original Hold-era values
Expected Result: pnr, bookingToken, and gdsPNR returned by BookAfterHold are byte-identical to the values from Hold; any change is treated as a defect.

Title: [BookAfterHold][Request] Validate BookAfterHold is rejected when attempted on an expired hold.

Notes: voidCapability is a per-booking, live, time-boxed flag, not a static per-supplier setting -- section 4.2's Void column tells you what to expect before booking, this flag tells you what's true for this specific booking right now.

Title: [CancelAfterHold] Verify CancelAfterHold is the least-validated endpoint in the API, with zero test-script coverage and no genuine saved example response in either version.

Title: [CancelAfterHold][Request] Validate CancelAfterHold is rejected when attempted against an already-booked (non-held) PNR.

Title: [Search]&[FareConfirm] [Response] Verify the generic pre-flow capability-confirmation procedure -- Search's per-offer flags re-confirmed at FareConfirm -- before scheduling any flow against a given supplier.

Title: [Search]&[FareConfirm]&[Book]&[Hold]&[Retrieve]&[FareConfirmAfterHold]&[BookAfterHold] [Response] Verify the V1-vs-V2 price-reconciliation script-coverage asymmetry across the shared endpoint set.

Notes: Foundational, first-round-priority exploratory case -- literally every endpoint in the API needs this confirmed before any other negative test can assert 'the right error' instead of just 'a rejection occurred'.
